description: WHY NOT A SHARED PRESET: rackctl/.github publishes none, so there is nothing to extend. This is a small, single-purpose static site — Astro + Starlight, a private theme package, two fontsource families and a lint/typecheck toolchain. Inheriting a platform preset would arrive with rules for gomod, helm and k8s.io that match nothing here.

TITLE CONTRACT: 'deps' is the semantic SCOPE, never the semantic TYPE. The repo's history is conventional (ci(deploy):, fix(docs):, docs(configuration):); a 'deps:' type sits outside the conventional set and would be unmergeable behind any title gate, silently, because a repo without such a gate merges it happily.

hostRules.description: Credentials for the @shuttering scope, which .npmrc maps to GitHub Packages. matchHost must be the full URL with its trailing slash so it agrees with the registryUrl .npmrc supplies; a bare hostname does not match and the lookup falls back to npmjs, where this scope publishes behind.

description: Astro and Starlight move as ONE PR. @astrojs/starlight declares a peer range on astro (currently ^7.0.0), so bumping astro across a major without starlight — or the reverse — produces a lockfile that cannot resolve. Separate PRs would each be green in isolation and break on merge order.

The @shuttering/* packages resolve from npm.pkg.github.com (see .npmrc), read with the hostRules token above. Pinned exact, like biome and for a stronger reason: this is a private design system, a bump can change how every page renders, and a caret is what let a broken theme version sit installed while a fix was already published. An exact pin forces a visible PR.
npmjs carries this scope too, but behind. A version this repo cannot see is a credential problem, never a reason to repoint the registry.
Typefaces are content, not behaviour: a fontsource bump changes glyph files, never an API. Group and automerge on minor/patch to keep them out of the review queue.
Biome is pinned to an exact version on purpose — the lockfile, not a range, is what makes CI's lint gate reproducible. Renovate should still move that pin, just visibly and on its own.
Pinned action SHAs and versions are a supply-chain control, including the osv-scanner gate itself. Keep them current — a stale scanner is a scanner that has stopped finding things.
fast-uri and postcss are held in pnpm.overrides to clear advisories osv-scanner gates on. Renovate may raise them; it must never drop below the pinned floor, which the override itself enforces.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes bypass the weekly schedule — osv-scanner already fails CI on a known advisory, so a held security bump blocks every unrelated PR too.
